title: Documents and Nodes
description: Documents are source texts; node parsers split them into Nodes (chunks) with metadata and relationships (parent/child, prev/next). Nodes are the retrieval unit. Hierarchical nodes let queries zoom from summary to detail.

title: VectorStoreIndex: the flagship
description: VectorStoreIndex embeds nodes and stores them in a vector DB; at query time it retrieves top-k similar nodes for the LLM. It is the standard RAG index and the default starting point. Most LlamaIndex apps begin here.

title: Query engines
description: Query engines wrap an index with retrieval + synthesis: retrieve nodes, then generate an answer with citations. Custom query engines compose retrievers, rerankers, and synthesizers. The engine is where RAG behavior is tuned.

title: Response synthesizers
description: Synthesizers control how retrieved nodes become answers: compact (stuff), tree summarize, or refine iteratively. Choice trades context usage against answer quality. Synthesis strategy is a first-class tuning knob.

title: Routers: choosing the right index
description: Routers send a query to the best index/tool (SQL vs vector vs summary) using an LLM selector or rules. Multi-index apps need routing because no single index fits every question. Routing is the orchestrator's job.

title: Ingestion pipelines
description: IngestionPipeline chains transformations (parse, embed, dedupe) with caching, so re-ingesting only processes changed documents. Pipelines make large corpora manageable and repeatable. Cache-backed ingestion is the production pattern.

title: Metadata filters and auto retrieval
description: Auto-retrieval has the LLM generate metadata filters (date ranges, categories) from the query, combining vector similarity with structured filtering. Filters make retrieval precise where pure similarity is fuzzy. Hybrid retrieval wins on real corpora.

title: Evaluation modules

title: Agents on top of indexes

title: Storage context and persistence
description: StorageContext bundles vector store, docstore, and index store; persist() saves everything to disk and reloads it later. Persistence separates slow indexing from fast serving. Build once, serve many times.

title: Reranking integrations
